evidence: log loss +0.0143 (95% interval -0.0033 to +0.0286). No demonstrable difference from the market's closing probabilities yet (the interval includes zero), and the point estimate favours the market.

102 picks, ROI -2.1% (95% interval -21.1% to +15.2%), win rate 57.8% against a break-even 58.3%. Random sides at the same margin match or beat this 39% of the time. Line movement toward the pick after it was made: +0.08 probability points on average (zero means no closing-line value).
How many bets before ROI can be trusted

At the observed spread of results, detecting a true 3% ROI takes about 5,049 bets and a 5% ROI about 1,818; a 1% edge takes 45,436. Closing-line value converges much faster, which is why it is the primary measure.
147 picks, ROI -6.2% (-14.9% to +3.5%): insufficient evidence (interval spans 0).
15 picks, ROI -100.0% (-100.0% to -100.0%): too few picks (<30) to say anything.
